questions.question: What cookie flags should you set for security? (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite)
questions.title: Secure Cookie Flags — HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What cookie flags should you set for security? (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite)?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser, network, and server contract (headers, cookies, streams)), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** HttpOnly: blocks JS access; Secure: HTTPS-only; SameSite=Lax/Strict: mitigates CSRF; Domain/Path: scope; __Host-/__Secure- prefixes.

**Classic weak answer:** Setting Secure without HTTPS in production — the cookie will be silently dropped by browsers.

**Senior finish:** Mention the __Host- prefix (enforces Secure + path=/ + no domain) as the strictest modern standard.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Secure Cookie Flags — HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What cookie flags should you set for security? (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite)

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **HttpOnly: blocks JS access; Secure: HTTPS-only; SameSite=Lax/Strict: mitigates CSRF; Domain/Path: scope; __Host-/__Secure- prefixes**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Setting Secure without HTTPS in production — the cookie will be silently dropped by browsers**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention the __Host- prefix (enforces Secure + path=/ + no domain) as the strictest modern standard**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** HttpOnly: blocks JS access; Secure: HTTPS-only; SameSite=Lax/Strict: mitigates CSRF; Domain/Path: scope; __Host-/__Secure- prefixes
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as Browser (SPA)
    participant I as Identity Provider
    participant B as BFF / API
    participant R as Resource API
    U->>I: Authorize (PKCE / code)
    I-->>U: Authorization code
    U->>B: Exchange code (server-side)
    B->>I: Token endpoint + client auth
    I-->>B: Access + refresh (optional)
    B-->>U: HttpOnly session cookie
    U->>R: API call (credentials include)
    Note over U,R: Tokens never in localStorage when using BFF pattern
```

sections.content:

| **Weak signal (avoid)** | Setting Secure without HTTPS in production — the cookie will be silently dropped by browsers |
| **Differentiator** | Mention the __Host- prefix (enforces Secure + path=/ + no domain) as the strictest modern standard |
| **Proof you shipped it** | Metrics (LCP, error rate), tests, DevTools trace, or incident story |

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **setting Secure without HTTPS in production — the cookie will be silently dropped by browsers** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** HttpOnly: blocks JS access; Secure: HTTPS-only; SameSite=Lax/Strict: mitigates CSRF; Domain/Path: scope; __Host-/__Secure- prefixes
- **Pitfall:** Setting Secure without HTTPS in production — the cookie will be silently dropped by browsers
- **Differentiator:** Mention the __Host- prefix (enforces Secure + path=/ + no domain) as the strictest modern standard
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **HttpOnly: blocks JS access; Secure: HTTPS-only; SameSite=Lax/Strict: mitigates CSRF; Domain/Path: scope; __Host-/__Secure- prefixes** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Setting Secure without HTTPS in production — the cookie will be silently dropped by browsers** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention the __Host- prefix (enforces Secure + path=/ + no domain) as the strictest modern standard**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
